My dad is a severe alcoholic and has a bunch of other health problems. So the talk of his will has come up a few times. He owns the house we currently live in, his (separated) wife's house, and a bar that has 2 apartments above it. As of now, his wife's house would remain her's or if she passes, go to their 3 children. The house we live in now, would be split amongst the 4 of us. The bar and the apartments would go solely to me. My mom is worried she won't get anything when he does pass away, so she constantly asks if I'll give her half of the bar. I personally want nothing to do with the bar due it being a cause for my parent's alcoholism. My mom says I should just give it all to her if that's the case. I would ask her to at least buy out my half, but she has been mentally abusive to me for most of my life, and constantly sabotaged anything I've done to try and better my own life. I've recently thought about just selling my quarter of the house to my siblings, and the entire bar to them or anyone else who wants it. WIBTA if I decided to leave my mom out of anything I get from my dad's will?

Let me start by understanding the scenario better. First, my family is quite large. Both of my parents have three kids from past relationships, and I'm their only child together. My dad is 71 and has been with my mom for 25 years, but he never divorced his previous wife. He's a severe alcoholic with other health issues, which probably makes the topic of his will a sensitive one. From what I gather, my dad owns three properties: the house we currently live in, his separated wife's house, and a bar with two apartments above it. The separated wife's house would go to her or her three children if she passes away. The house we live in would be split among the four of usâĢĶmy mom, my siblings, and me. The bar and the apartments would go solely to me. My mom is worried she won't get anything when my dad passes away, so she keeps asking if I'll give her half of the bar. I don't want anything to do with the bar because it's a cause of my parents' alcoholism. My mom suggests I should just give it all to her, but I want at least to sell my half. However, she's been mentally abusive to me for most of my life and has sabotaged anything I've tried to do to better my own life. I'm thinking about selling my quarter of the house to my siblings and the entire bar to them or anyone else who wants it. The question is, is it wrong for me to decide to leave my mom out of anything I get from my dad's will? Okay, so I need to break this down. Legally, does my dad's will dictate how everything is split? If the will says the house is split among the four of us, then legally, I have a quarter share. The bar and apartments are solely mine. So, legally, I have the right to sell my share. But morally, is it wrong to leave my mom out? She's been mentally abusive, and she's worried about not getting anything. On one hand, she's been a bad parent, but on the other hand, she's still my mom, and she's worried about her future. I also need to consider the impact on my siblings. If I sell my share to them, how will that affect our relationships? Will they be okay with me selling it, or will they feel like I'm taking advantage of the situation? Additionally, there's the aspect of the bar being a symbol of my parents' alcoholism. I don't want to be associated with that, which is a valid reason for wanting to sell it. But does that justify cutting my mom out entirely? I also need to think about the financial implications. If I sell my share, will I be able to get a fair price? Or will I be undervaluing my share because of the emotional baggage attached to it? Another thing to consider is whether there's a way to compromise. Maybe instead of giving her half of the bar, I could offer her a different asset or some financial support. But given her history of mental abuse and sabotage, I might not feel comfortable doing that. I also wonder if there's a legal way to ensure that my mom doesn't get anything from my dad's will. If the will is clear about how everything is split, then legally, I don't have control over what she gets. But if I'm selling my share, I can choose who to sell it to, which could exclude her. But is that fair? If the will says the house is split among the four of us, and I sell my share to my siblings, then effectively, my mom is left with nothing. Is that what I want? It feels like a way to punish her for her past behavior, but is that the right approach? I also need to think about the bigger picture. How will this decision affect me in the long run? If I cut my mom out, will that create more family tension? Or will it give me the closure I need to move forward? In summary, I'm torn between my legal rights to sell my share and my moral obligations to my mom, despite her past behavior. I need to weigh the legal, emotional, and relational aspects to decide what's right or wrong in this situation.
